title: Young`s demonstrative translation of scientific secrets or a collection of above 500 useful receipts on a variety of subjects
summary: A practical compendium of household, craft, and trade recipes, first printed in Toronto in 1861 by Rowsell & Ellis and entered for copyright under Daniel Young. The book collects more than five hundred "receipts" (instructions) on a wide range of subjects. Its sections cover decorative painting on glass and wood, transfer varnishes, electroplating of gold and silver, gilding of metal, glass and porcelain, bookbinding edges, metal silvering and coppering, dyeing cloth, straw and silk, and the making of coloured enamels and glass stains. Alongside the technical recipes are miscellaneous remedies, some of which are dangerous by modern standards, and a closing series of proverbs on thrift, debt, and prudence. This text is a modern typed transcription made by Paul Hubbs and a nephew in 1987 to 1990 from a family copy, with the front matter and editorial notes describing that process. The excerpts shown are the opening, a middle section on dyeing and glass colours, and the closing aphorisms and note to purchasers.
